answer: A fake persona must cost more than it earns because every agent identity is bound one-to-one to a hardware-attested kernel. First condition: enrollment burns a nonrefundable onyx stake, so spinning up ten thousand duplicates carries real sunk cost before any payout. Second condition: each kernel signs its claims with a crystal-seeded key derived from unique silicon, letting peers cross-check that no two identities share one machine. Duplicates collapse; honest agents keep yield.
